A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AKOrN research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original object-discovery, Sudoku-solving, and CIFAR10 robustness and calibration experiments, including additional results and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Shapes experiments, architectural ablations, sensitivity analyses, runtime measurements, and further baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The core Kuramoto updates, connectivity mechanisms, and training objectives remain. However, v2 Table 19 introduces prediction selection using summed energies across timesteps, extending v1's final-state energy voting. Appendix C.2 also changes the reported Sudoku readout from Batch Normalization, ReLU, and linear layers to ReLU and linear layers; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects rerunning experiments or correcting documentation.

E1.justification: v2 adds the authors' Shapes dataset to object discovery: images containing two to four potentially overlapping objects drawn from four basic shapes. The existing synthetic and natural-image datasets, Sudoku distributions, and CIFAR10 scenarios remain. This is a limited expansion within an existing task.

E2.justification: v2 adds Energy Transformer and symmetrized AKOrN to Sudoku comparisons, Gaussian-noise-trained ResNets to robustness comparisons, and ItrConv to the extended CIFAR10 table. Table 18 additionally compares Rotating Features on PascalVOC and NSI on COCO2017. These substantially broaden the alternatives evaluated across the paper's principal tasks.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes Sudoku energy voting from 100 to 4,096 samples at 128 steps. However, v2 Table 19 assigns the same 89.5% result to 1,000 samples and 512 steps, leaving its exact protocol unresolved. New dimensionality, depth, component-control, and runtime experiments substantially expand evaluation design. Figure 11 also revises the stated baseline MLP width from four to two times the channel size, without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing positional-encoding, up-tiling, noise, and natural-frequency analyses, v2 Appendix A adds projection removal, replacement with residual updates, dimensionality sweeps, training-loss analyses, bias/readout-norm ablations, and runtime comparisons. Appendix D.4 adds symmetry controls, while Table 16 and Figures 26 and 31 add depth comparisons and overlapping-object failure cases.

E5.justification: Synthetic object-discovery results previously reported as point estimates now include means and standard deviations, with Tables 14, 15, and 17 specifying three weight-initialization seeds. Uncertainty is also added to cited baseline entries where available. Sudoku's five-seed reporting remains; Table 19 newly discloses exclusion of one failed symmetrized-AKOrN run. These are reporting changes, not evidence of an explicit increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Many synthetic-object scores change: Tetrominoes FG-ARI changes from 86.19 versus 86.81 for AKOrNattn and ItrSA to 88.6 versus 85.8, reversing their ordering. Headline Sudoku OOD accuracy changes from 61.1±14.7 to 89.5±2.5 under revised, inconsistently documented conditions, so this is not a controlled same-setting gain. Shapes, ablation, baseline, and runtime results add substantial evidence; the main natural-image and CIFAR10 Table 4 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (3) gains a factor of one-half on the pairwise interaction term. Section 3 narrows its example Lyapunov conditions from general symmetric coupling blocks to scalar multiples of the identity. New Appendices F and G supply a derivation and propositions involving commutator and normality conditions for non-increasing energy. These materially revise the mathematical justification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the broad contributions in object binding, reasoning, robustness, and calibration. Novelty positioning changes locally: Section 3 stops calling the symmetry-breaking term novel, while Section 5 explicitly claims the first standalone scaling of a synchrony-based model to natural images.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations and applicability boundaries: it diagnoses underfitting at N=2, discusses degradation at large dimensions and under symmetric constraints, and identifies failures on overlapping Shapes objects. It also interprets energy voting as energy-based-model behavior despite task-only training. Conversely, Figure 28 removes v1 Figure 18's qualification that all sampled predictions fail on approximately 30% of boards. The fixed-norm memory limitation remains.

D1.justification: Existing training recipes and repository access largely remain. v2 adds Shapes construction and hyperparameters, implementation details for the CIFAR10 ItrConv comparator, runtime measurements and their measurement definitions, and a project-page link. The existing up-tiling code receives partial variable corrections, although its malformed final reshape statement remains.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially broadens coverage of historical oscillatory networks, learned Kuramoto synchronization, graph-based oscillator models, and spiking synchrony. It develops a more specific comparison with Energy Transformer. Section 3 adds generalized-Kuramoto predecessors, and Figure 2 acknowledges related recurrent architectures. These changes expand and refine research positioning beyond bibliographic date corrections.

P1.justification: Most main-text organization and wording remain. v2 fixes the malformed Section 6.3 heading and opening, clarifies layer indexing, expands metric and up-tiling explanations, and rewrites related-work passages. Earlier physics and robustness discussions become Appendix B.1/B.2, and the rotating-dimension discussion moves from the conclusion into the appendices. The additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the network diagram and adds projection, sensitivity, loss, runtime, corruption-example, and failure-case displays. Figure 3 gains Shapes and error bars; Figure 7 expands its sampling axis and removes the majority-voting curve. Tables gain uncertainty displays and new comparison structures. Many earlier cluster visualizations are retained and renumbered rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper through controlled tests of its central architectural choices, uncertainty reporting for previously single-valued object-discovery results, and expanded formal support for the energy argument. These address important gaps in v1's evidential and mathematical foundation. The conflicting Sudoku budgets in Tables 3 and 19 weaken reproducibility of the headline result, but the broader gains remain substantial; the higher reported accuracy alone does not establish improvement.
